rv.q: The new show at Red Orchid Theatre turns out to be a gorgeous little 90-minute two-hander, a beautifully acted and directed father-daughter play...
The title of play may allude to birds, but the heart of the show is a duo who love each other and struggle to communicate.
BIRDS OF NORTH AMERICA is an exquisite emotional experience that may bring tears to your eyes.
A DELICATE CHAMBER PIECE THAT WILL BREAK YOUR HEART
This is a beautiful play filled with honest human emotions.
This piece drills down to the essence of them all, managing to capture something deeply personal while being sweepingly universal and hauntingly specific.
While a two-hander on a single set could be boring, Fitzgerald's superb direction makes every moment meaningful.

Like love and birdwatching, the script by Anna Ouyang Moench is patient, gradually accumulating weight and resonance until you find yourself misty-eyed watching people you didn’t know ninety minutes ago.
The duo captivate in navigating the messiness of a parent-adult child relationship.
The exquisitely acted two-hander covers a decade in the relationship of a father and daughter.
Our two actors, Judd and Mason forge a believable poignant relationship on stage.
Birds of North America is a tender portrait that walks the taut line between pain and sentimentality with the vivid humor of recognition.
Birds of North America is one of those plays you really don't want to miss.
It all came together in a beautifully presented piece of theatre.
This is a moving, tender, complex play, masterful in the portrayal of character and communication.
From its opening moments to its final scenes, Birds of North America delivers a family drama filled with humor, heart, and emotional honesty.

cn.t: Critics praise this intimate father-daughter drama for its emotional depth and powerful performances, particularly John Judd's. The quiet, reflective story about family bonds through birdwatching resonates as a beautifully crafted chamber piece.
